## Inclusion rule

See the header comment in `tools/harvest-hermes-lit.ts` for the full rule.
Short version: a file is harvested only if (1) it has a plain
`%hermes ... | %FileCheck` RUN line (not a compiler/bytecode-dump
invocation, not a negative/expect-failure test, not gated behind an
experimental `-X...` flag), (2) every `// CHECK...` directive it uses is
one of `CHECK`/`CHECK-NEXT`/`CHECK-LABEL`/`CHECK-EMPTY` (linear,
literal-text semantics — `CHECK-NOT`/`CHECK-DAG`/`CHECK-SAME`/
`CHECK-COUNT` and `{{...}}` regexes are not representable as a plain
expected.txt), (3) it never touches `HermesInternal`, and (4) running it
under Node (RUN/CHECK comments stripped, print shim prepended) produces
stdout that **exactly** matches the CHECK-derived expected.txt — this is
an empirical filter, not just a syntactic one, so lit tests whose Hermes
output differs from Node's (numeric formatting, Symbol/Proxy/property-order
edge cases, non-strict-mode divergences) are excluded rather than harvested
with a wrong expected.txt.
